clue.text: Investing round figure in boring club is a punt?

parts.note: flat means dull or boring

indicators.note: to invest something in a place is to put it inside, so the round figure goes into the run of letters after 'in'

parts.note: a bat is a club used to hit a ball
O is the round figure zero

explanation.surface: A golfer wonders whether putting a number on a dull club amounts to a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punt' looks like a bet; here it is the flat-bottomed river boat. 'Investing' puts O inside FLATBAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A punt is a kind of shallow, flat-bottomed boat poled along a river, so it is one example of the type.

clue.text: Five last works for religious celebration

indicators.note: 'works' read as a verb means the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A list of a composer's final five works chosen for a church feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like a noun (compositions) but is the anagram signal on FIVE LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A festival is a feast day or holy celebration, such as those in the church calendar.

clue.text: Scaremongering member divides elite group

indicators.note: a piece that divides another splits it, sitting inside it

parts.note: the A-list is the group of top celebrities
an arm is a limb, or member, of the body

explanation.surface: One member spreading panic splits an exclusive clique.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarmist person or remark spreads needless fear, which is what scaremongering means.

clue.text: Family bathroom designed primarily to accommodate toilet

indicators.note: to accommodate is to hold, so the other piece goes inside
primarily means the first letters of the preceding words are taken

parts.note: loo is a British word for a toilet

explanation.surface: A family bathroom planned from the start around where the toilet will go.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood means lineage or kin, as in 'blood is thicker than water'.

clue.text: American behind position supporting international aid

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece that supports another sits below it

parts.note: ass is the American word for the backside
a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: Behind an American stance backing international aid lies a diplomatic picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance is help or support, the same thing as aid.

clue.text: Tense opening of play about plan of action?

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
Act I opens a play
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A tense first act of a drama leads to talk of a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening of play' gives a whole stage section, ACT I, not just a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned manoeuvre for reaching a goal.

clue.text: Plot many intended to be overheard

indicators.note: overheard means we use how the phrase sounds when spoken

parts.note: many is 'a lot', intended is 'meant', together A LOT MEANT

explanation.surface: A conspiracy that many people meant to be eavesdropped on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a scheme; it is a patch of land. ALLOTMENT is a small rented garden plot, common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a small piece of land rented for growing vegetables, a plot.

clue.text: Heart shown by benevolent examiner?

definitions.meaning: an examiner who ticks answers rather than crossing them out is kind

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted marker showing generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is informal slang for the heart, from its beat, and one who marks answers right ticks them.

clue.text: Howler by athletics supremo about game making a comeback

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: Sebastian Coe, Olympic champion, heads World Athletics

indicators.note: coming back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to toy with something is to play a game with it; a toy is a plaything

explanation.surface: A sports boss commits an embarrassing blunder as a game returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Howler' looks like a gaffe; it is an animal that howls. Lord Coe is a British athlete and head of world athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: The coyote is an American wild dog famous for its howling at night.

clue.text: Fish recognise husky by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase tells us to use the spoken sound of the words before

parts.note: recognise is 'see', husky meaning gravel-voiced is 'hoarse': SEE HOARSE

explanation.surface: Spotting a husky dog, or a husky voice, by the sound it makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husky' looks like the sled dog but means hoarse-voiced.
explanation.definitionFit: The seahorse is a small upright marine fish with a horse-like head.

clue.text: Losing pawn in this game would be fortunate

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn
lucky means fortunate

explanation.surface: A chess player notes that dropping a pawn here would be a lucky break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing pawn in this' says the answer minus P gives 'fortunate', so the answer is P plus LUCKY. 'game' looks like a pastime but is the adjective meaning brave.
explanation.definitionFit: Game as an adjective means willing and brave, just as plucky does.

clue.text: Shameless married types having sex outside

indicators.note: the sex piece is put outside, around the other letters

parts.note: 'it' is a coy word for sex
modes are types or kinds

explanation.surface: Brazen married couples making love outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Immodest means lacking decency or modesty, so without shame.

clue.text: What would be narrower if it weren't tree-lined?

definitions.text: What would be narrower if it weren't tree-lined?

parts.words: What would be narrower if it weren't tree-lined?
parts.note: the word has TREE lined by S and T; take it away and the short form ST is left, a narrower word

explanation.walkthrough: A road is wider with no trees; but the word itself is S-TREE-T, and without the tree only ST, its abbreviation, remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a town road, often lined with trees along its pavements.

clue.text: State demonstrating prompt dispatch of minor punishment by guards

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: by means times, as in three by four
lines are sentences a pupil must write out as a small punishment

explanation.surface: A sentence about quickly getting through a petty penalty under supervision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link but gives TIMES; LINES are a British school punishment of writing a sentence many times.
explanation.definitionFit: Timeliness is the quality of happening at the right moment, so promptness.

clue.text: As a voice it's possibly helping to form union

indicators.note: possibly says these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A singer's voice possibly helps build a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Associative describes what links or joins things into an association.

clue.text: What I fed to angry social worker?

definitions.text: What I fed to angry social worker?

indicators.note: fed to means given inside, so the letter goes into the word

parts.note: cross means angry
an ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: Someone asks what pastry they gave to a cross ant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' sounds like a care professional but is the ant.
explanation.definitionFit: A croissant is a flaky breakfast pastry, the food fed in the scene.

clue.text: Suspicious inscription on unknown soldier's tomb?

explanation.walkthrough: A PARA is a paratrooper; 'no ID' says he is unknown, so the answer splits as PARA NO ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Paranoid means excessively mistrustful of others.

clue.text: Deranged Prince subdued following the Queen's intervention

indicators.note: an intervention comes between, so the royal letters go in between the other two pieces

parts.note: muted means subdued
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen; 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A mad prince calmed down after the Queen stepped in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deranged' looks like mad; it is the literal sense, arranged differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Permuted means arranged in another order, the literal sense of deranged.

clue.text: Cast three actors to create parts for musical?

indicators.note: to cast is to shape, so the letters are moulded into a new order

explanation.surface: A director casts three actors and creates roles for a stage musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like hiring actors and 'parts' like roles, but the parts are instrumental lines.
explanation.definitionFit: To orchestrate is to write out a score for the instruments of an orchestra.

clue.text: University rector inspired by person who employs one taking excessive interest

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so the first pieces go inside

parts.note: a user is one who employs something

explanation.surface: A college rector inspired by a nosy employer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' looks like curiosity but means interest charged on loans.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at extortionate rates.

clue.text: Conclusion of modernist composer's tour

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its last letter

parts.note: Maurice Ravel was a French composer; 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: The finale of a modern composer's concert tour.
explanation.definitionFit: To tour is to travel around a place.

clue.text: Pressure beginning to tell on son aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: re means on or about

explanation.surface: Strain grows on board as someone must break news to their son.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is strain or pressure, physical or mental.

clue.text: Deny record demand following merger

indicators.note: the two words merge, sharing a letter where they meet, so one copy is dropped

parts.note: a disc is a record
claim means demand

explanation.surface: A firm denies a record claim after a business merger.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclaim is to renounce or refuse to accept a claim, to deny it.

clue.text: Coat of cashmere lined with one material or another

indicators.note: lined with means the other piece is put inside
the coat of a word is its outside letters

parts.note: rep is a corded fabric

explanation.surface: A cashmere coat lined with some fabric or other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one material' is REP; 'or another' is the answer, a different fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepe is a crinkled fabric, a second material beside rep.

clue.text: Celebrate hosting penultimate part of chat show

indicators.note: to host is to hold, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: revel means celebrate

indicators.note: the penultimate part is the last letter but one

explanation.surface: Partying on a chat show while hosting its second-to-last segment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' looks like a TV programme; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to show or disclose something.

clue.text: Injury restricts footballer backing transfer immediately

indicators.note: restricts means encloses, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong or injury in law

indicators.note: backing means read backwards

parts.note: Pelé was a great Brazilian footballer

explanation.surface: An injury blocks a footballer's quick transfer to a new club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transfer' looks like a club deal; it is moving instantly, as in science fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: To teleport is to move instantaneously from one place to another, as in science fiction.

clue.text: Half-hearted teller ordered checks for each recount

indicators.note: checks means holds back, enclosing
ordered means put into a new order
the heart of the word is its double L; half of it is lost

parts.note: a, as in 'a pound a head', means for each

explanation.surface: A lukewarm bank teller is told to check figures for each recount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' drops one L of the central LL; 'ordered' rearranges TELER into RELTE, and 'checks' puts A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to recount or narrate it.

clue.text: Went upstairs perhaps when clubs closed

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
C is the card abbreviation for clubs
ended means closed or finished

explanation.surface: Someone went upstairs when the nightclubs shut.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to climb, and going upstairs is one example.
